about: The voxel contract's junction matrix (docs/building-voxels.md, D348) as data. Each row is a junction, the rule that closes it, the code that implements the rule, and what proves it: tests by module path under crates/terra_build (`tests::rules` is tests/rules.rs) and cases of the scene registry (`terra_build::scenes::registry`) the mesh checker's ratchet holds, each a part of a registered scene's name, at least one scene it names in a group the ratchet's baseline holds at no fault. `node tools/docs/docs.ts --render` writes the page's matrix from this file; the docs check fails if the page differs, and terra_build's test `every_row_of_the_voxel_contract_is_proved` fails if a row's code, test or case is missing.

rows.junction: Side by side, in a run
rows.rule: Block: faces between culled, one surface. Coursed: a log a course along the run
cases: logs: rectangle, gable roof

rows.junction: A free end
rows.rule: Arris up it; logs cut flush, every other course a hair short

rows.junction: L, outside and inside
rows.rule: Arris and Inside, crests mitred out and back; logs interlock by axis, half a course apart
cases: L, gable roof

rows.junction: T and cross
rows.rule: The through wall runs on, no joint where another crosses
cases: T, gable roof
U, gable roof

rows.junction: Walls of different heights; a wall's top
rows.rule: A crest where nothing is over it

rows.junction: A wall two or three thick, a pier
rows.rule: Block: one mass, an opening's head sunk behind each face's lintel through its cube. Coursed: skins along the faces, crossing only at the ends (D263); a solid mass's top a deck whose rims meet at its corners, the one along the joists' ends running through and the other butting it; where a pier or wall rises from the mass, the deck's rim runs on into it under its members, and its corner posts run down past the deck, and at a free end on to the ground
cases: junction, a thick wall with a window

rows.junction: A post in a wall, or alone
rows.rule: A column alone is a post: one upright; a wall's logs stop at it
cases: junction, a roof on posts

rows.junction: Two cubes of a kind meeting only along an edge
rows.rule: Neither dresses the shared edge; each turns round its own outside corner there, its part in the wall mitred out and its part out of the face cut at the plane halfway between the two
cases: junction, cubes meeting along an upright edge
junction, cubes meeting along a level edge

rows.junction: Every edge with a role
rows.rule: Dressed once, by its owner

rows.junction: Heavier and lighter, in an L, a T or in line
rows.rule: The heavier runs through, quoined; the lighter ends with its end board
cases: logs with stone: rectangle, gable roof
logs with stone: T, hip roof

rows.junction: Lighter on heavier (logs on a stone plinth)
rows.rule: The heavier's cap (`Meet`)
cases: village: timber on a masonry plinth house

rows.junction: Heavier on lighter
rows.rule: Its foot does not sink over the lighter

rows.junction: As heavy as each other (logs and hewn)
rows.rule: Each ends with its own end board
cases: hewn with logs: rectangle, gable roof
hewn with logs: L, gable roof

rows.junction: A wall on another kind's footing
rows.rule: One plinth, the footing's

rows.junction: Walls or rooms crossing or overlapping
rows.rule: Not yet closed: a floor's boards in the plane of a log wall run along or through the room, an end board in the plane of a log's sawn end where a stone wall runs through a log room, floor boards in one another where two rooms overlap, a dressed stone in the plane of a board where a hewn wall runs into a carved stone room

rows.junction: A block of stone cut to a corner or a stair beside timber
rows.rule: Not yet closed: dressed stone 8 cm out of its cubes, or a fifth of it under the block surface's relief

rows.junction: A hole in a coursed wall
rows.rule: Courses end at it, framed with jambs, head and sill boards
cases: QA cabin

rows.junction: A hole in a block wall
rows.rule: Jamb stones, one lintel and one sill across its full width, the wall sunk behind them
cases: stone: rectangle, gable roof

rows.junction: Any carved shape; a notch at a foot or a top
rows.rule: Framed along its own edges
cases: QA cabin

rows.junction: A door or shutters fitted
rows.rule: The prop's own frame, sized to its hole; the kit lays none there

rows.junction: A hole whose top is a roof cube
rows.rule: The roof's cube is its head: a coursed wall's head board under it, cut a hair under the roof's deck (`trims::frames`); a block wall's opening closed by the roof's deck and the gable carried up either side, a lintel there standing through the covering at an eave
cases: roofs and walls: openings up to a roof

rows.junction: An opening or a carve at a timber wall's corner
rows.rule: Not yet closed: a window at a room's corner tile, or a box carved through a corner at its foot, leaves a jamb or head board a centimetre out of its cubes

rows.junction: A floor under a wall
rows.rule: Block: a border inside, a foot outside. Deck: boards run on under the members past where they stand back at their narrowest (`layout::member_face`), and beside round logs a strip under their edge on past a log bowed its furthest away; or they stop at another kind's. A thick wall's cubes beside a floor are walls drawn to their face, never its mass's undrawn inside; no slot between a floor's boards and a wall beside them
cases: village: masonry and timber house of two storeys

rows.junction: A floor's open edge
rows.rule: Block: rounded, flagged; deck: a rim, joists where in the air
cases: junction, a floor with a stairwell and a balcony

rows.junction: A floor with a stairwell, or reaching past the wall under it
rows.rule: Block: soffit and rounding. Deck: rims round the hole and the overhang, butting at their corners; out over the air, open under its joists as a deck is
cases: junction, a floor with a stairwell and a balcony

rows.junction: A deck on posts; a post's top in a deck
rows.rule: Bearers on the posts, joists, rim (D306); the post's top cube is the deck's. A rail of the deck's own members stands on it, boarded under; its rims run on into the posts rising at its corners, and its boards under each post past where it stands back at its narrowest (`layout::member_face`); no slot between its boards and a post beside them
cases: village: squared timber lookout deck on posts

rows.junction: Stairs onto a deck, and from the ground
rows.rule: Stringers bear on the deck's rim and the ground; a stringer's head a hair under the deck's top, the deck's boards not run on over the flight's top step
cases: QA cabin

rows.junction: Stairs against a wall
rows.rule: The flight's own stringer or stone beside the wall's face; a stone stair's nose reaching back no further than its step and a hair into what rises behind it
cases: junction, stairs against a wall

rows.junction: A cut cube beside a whole one
rows.rule: A cut side shows over a lower cut; copings run on and mitre at a ramp's head and foot
cases: junction, stairs against a wall

rows.junction: A timber cube boarded as a box: upside down, an upper half, a corner slope
rows.rule: Butt joints, as a carpenter boxes it: the courses of a side facing east or west run through to the cube's edges; every other board ending or edging where a side is clad (a course facing north or south, a top or underside board, a riser) stops against that cladding's inside face; a raking underside's head stops under the top's deck and its foot, cut plumb, at the cladding inside the side it falls to

rows.junction: A boarded timber cube on a wall or a floor
rows.rule: Not yet closed: an inner corner slope on a log room's wall shows sky past it, an upside-down slope beside a log wall's window has a log in the plane of its boards, and far off a deck's board ends in the plane of a corner slope's cladding over it

rows.junction: A deck against another kind's deck or wall
rows.rule: Not yet closed: a deck's log ends in the plane of another kind's deck's, a post's log over the roof beside an eave, sky through a stone room's far drawing beside a deck

rows.junction: Stairs or a ramp against a wall or up to a doorway
rows.rule: Not yet closed: a log's sawn end under a ramp's block surface; a board in the plane of the floor at a doorway a flight comes up to

sections.title: Walls and roofs
sections.intro: Every row here is also a row of the roof–wall design's table, each a row of the kit sheet (`--sheet-rows "roofs and walls"`) and a base of the checker's *roofs and walls* family (`roof_walls`) in each wall kit under each roof, at every detail.

rows.junction: A wall under a roof cube: a gable, the wedge under an eave
rows.rule: Carried up to the deck: a block surface cut at it, courses cut to the slope, eave blocking cut to the roof; no dress at the gable's steps
cases: rectangle, gable roof
rectangle, hip roof

rows.junction: A roof's frame at a wall
rows.rule: Stops at the wall's face, never through a gable or out under a verge

rows.junction: Logs reaching a roof
rows.rule: Cut where the roof begins

rows.junction: A roof on a cut wall cube or on posts
rows.rule: The roof stands on it; nothing to carry up
cases: junction, a roof on posts
junction, a roof on cut wall cubes

rows.junction: A roof against a wall upslope (a lean-to's head)
rows.rule: An apron (`Flashing`); the covering tucked 15 cm into the wall (R3)
cases: roofs and walls: a roof rising to a wall

rows.junction: A roof's verge against a wall
rows.rule: Steps (`Step`) along the sloping edge, the covering tucked
cases: roofs and walls: a verge against a wall

rows.junction: A roof falling to a wall (an eave or a hip's end against it)
rows.rule: A back gutter (`Gutter`), the covering tucked; the wall under the edge stops under the roof where it comes down to its top, blocked to the roof (its own blocking, into the corner where a crossing row's would leave the space against the wall open), and runs on in the wall beyond, every other course a hair short there as at a free end (`runs::under_roofs`)
cases: roofs and walls: a roof falling to a wall

rows.junction: A valley or inside corner at a wall; a hip or ridge at a wall
rows.rule: R4: the board along the north and south butts the other's side in an inside corner, each stops at an outside one; a crease's cap ends uncapped at the face; a board narrowed where the roof folds away under it
cases: roofs and walls: a roof in the corner of two walls
roofs and walls: on hips and valleys

rows.junction: A wall or chimney up through a slope, a ridge or an eave (beside roof cubes)
rows.rule: The covering tucked into it on every side and flashed: an apron below, steps up its sides, a back gutter above (R3, R4); a timber wall's end board against another kind's chimney stops at the roof's cube and is carried up into it cut under the deck (`trims::ends`); a chimney's dress over the roof is its own, not a piece through the roof
cases: roofs and walls: through a roof
roofs and walls: a chimney of another kind in a gable

rows.junction: A wall on a roof cube: on a slope, a corner, a ridge, a hip, a valley; a storey on the eaves
rows.rule: The roof whole under it (R1), it carried down to the deck: a block surface cut there, a timber curb (R2); its foot flashed; the hull draws the roof cube whole (R6); held as any cube is (R7)
cases: roofs and walls: standing on a roof
roofs and walls: on hips and valleys
roofs and walls: a storey over a roof
roofs and walls: shapes on a roof
roofs and walls: going up

rows.junction: A roof's eave over timber walls whichever way it falls, a room's flat top beside them
rows.rule: The courses left out under it blocked to the roof whichever axis its wall runs along; a row leaves a corner to the crossing row's blocking only where that row is a wall under the eave too, never a floor or a flat top beside it, nor a gable the roof rises along, where its own blocking runs on into the corner

rows.junction: A lean-to's high corner over a timber gable rising north or south
rows.rule: Not yet closed: over the gable's crest at the high wall's corner a slot 5 cm high is left between the eave blocking's weather face and the wall's

rows.junction: Ridge, hip, valley; a ridge a cube wide
rows.rule: Creases between squares, capped once; a modelled cap's faces cut to length or joined to its cap, never left over one another
cases: L, hip roof

rows.junction: Eaves, verges and where they meet
rows.rule: Each open side exactly one edge piece; a hip's foot mitred; verges at an apex take no cap
cases: rectangle, hip roof

rows.junction: A wing's ridge into the main roof; a dormer
rows.rule: One roof: valleys where they meet, the wing's beam butting the main one
cases: L, gable roof
T, gable roof
U, gable roof
QA cabin

rows.junction: A roof over a roof, apart; an eave over a lower roof
rows.rule: Squares carry on only where their corners meet, so roofs at two heights stay apart
cases: QA cabin, its storey over its roof left on

rows.junction: Two roof kinds meeting
rows.rule: As one roof; each square in its own kind
cases: junction, two roof kinds meeting

rows.junction: A roof kind cut to a stair, an upper half or a post
rows.rule: Refused, "A roof is cut only to slopes, corners and halves." (`Shape::roofs`), by plan, reshape or change of kind

rows.junction: A hole carved in a roof
rows.rule: Something standing beside the roof to its squares, a cube or two across: flashed round, no eaves carried into it, open at every detail
cases: roofs and walls: holes in a roof

rows.junction: A roof kind's corner square laid by hand where no roof is
rows.rule: Its eaves carried on past each open side; round a corner of two open sides only as one plane or a hip's crease running down off the roof, never a valley out past an outside corner nor a crease rising out past the roof, so no beam or cap stands past its edge

rows.junction: A roof kind's whole or half square laid by hand on its own, its top level
rows.rule: No batten on a level square: no course's foot crosses it, so none is cut through its plane to lie along its triangles' edges and diagonals, crossing one another

rows.junction: A roof kind's corners laid by hand alike side by side, the roof stepping a cube between them
rows.rule: A hip's or a valley's beam at an end that meets no crease is brought back plumb inside its square, not carried past it by its drop under the slope; a cube's eaves are not carried round its corner from a side open over a lower roof of its own, where they stood a step over that roof's eaves, so no beam or trim stands over the lower roof

rows.junction: A roof kind's outer corners laid by hand alike side by side, the roof stepping down a cube past each peak
rows.rule: A hip's beam at a high end that meets no crease is brought back so far that its whole section, not only its line, is inside its square: its side and the foot of its sawn end stay off the lower roof past the corner, whether its drop under the slope or a wall it is cut at left its end at the peak

rows.junction: A roof kind's slopes or corners laid by hand alike side by side, the roof stepping down a cube from one's level top edge to the next
rows.rule: The higher cube's level edge at the step's top is an eave: its fascia hangs plumb out past it and boards close the step under it, as at the top of any step, standing up to the step's height over the lower roof. The check measures a roof's own piece within its edge's reach out past an eave from that eave, not from the roof below (Roofs::eave_over); a piece out past a sloping edge or a corner's peak is still measured from the roof under it

rows.junction: A roof kind laid by hand where no roof is: slopes and corners stacked two high, a wall standing across the step
rows.rule: No batten is laid under a face's course within its reach of a step's top, where the roof beyond is a lower one far under the face's plane carried on, as none is at a crest: the top batten's corner stood out past the step's edge and its end past the wall standing across the step, over the lower roof

rows.junction: A roof's eave over a wall running on past it, the wall's top at the eave
rows.rule: A level edge of the roof's own cubes with a whole wall cube past it, its top where the edge is, is against that wall: flashed, never an eave whose board stands on the wall's top past the eaves the wall stops (R4)

rows.junction: A roof square laid on another roof
rows.rule: Not yet closed: a corner square of one kind laid on a gable of another stands its board, covering and trims 8 cm out past both roofs' edges

rows.junction: A wall's foot on the ground or a slope
rows.rule: A plinth stepping a course at a time and run on down into it; footings to the cube the ground passes through, set into it
cases: rectangle, gable roof

rows.junction: A doorway above the ground
rows.rule: Door steps are cubes of the footing kind (D261)

rows.junction: Carving, a cube at a time
rows.rule: The kit lays itself again round the gap, cut and framed at the first cut
cases: QA cabin

rows.junction: A change of material
rows.rule: Within a pattern a repaint, the junctions unchanged (D298); across patterns the `meets` rows above
cases: QA cabin

rows.junction: Damage
rows.rule: A stone hole has sides and a back (D305); timber and roofs break in the shader
cases: rectangle under a gable, damaged
rows.also: the frames check's *damaged* (`cargo xtask artifacts --frames --checks damaged`): timber's and a roof's damage held still and shown

rows.junction: What is left after a collapse
rows.rule: Any arrangement is drawn (D192 rule 3); plans hanging from what fell go with it; a lintel left over air stops at its cube (`roles::End::Free`)
cases: rectangle under a gable, after a collapse

rows.junction: A section's edge
rows.rule: Pieces by anchor; a section is cut from the base laid whole

rows.junction: A plan; a building going up
rows.rule: What is in laid from what is built (D358): a top, an end and a corner where it stops, a cube going in a top at its fill, all laid away as it is built on; ghosts drawn from the plan; what is in hides what is not; a wall carried up into a roof's cube in with the roof's first stage, an upright in with its first cube
cases: rectangle under a gable, as a plan
rectangle under a gable, walls going up
rectangle under a gable, roof going on

rows.junction: Near, mid, far, hull
rows.rule: The same closed shape, coarser
cases: castle
rows.also: the checker inspects every case at all four details
